newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk c.bank head sees single-digit inflation aim.
newsitem.headline: Turk c.bank head sees single-digit inflation aim.

text.p: Turkey's central bank governor Gazi Ercel said the country's medium-term economic programme should have the aim of achieving single-digit inflation.
"A medium-term programme should have one aim: to bring inflation down to single digits," Ercel said at a seminar on Turkey and the European Union.
Turkish wholesale price inflation stood at an annual 78.6 percent in February.
Ercel said he expected inflation to be between 70 and 80 percent at the end of June despite the impact of public sector wage rises of 50-70 percent made so far this year.
"In spite of recent developments I believe it will be in the 70s (at the end of June)," he said.
Ercel said the Treasury had reached its short-term cash borrowing limit at the central bank which stands at six percent of the difference between the budget expenditure this year and last year.
The central banker said there were no technical problems in the development of an economic programme, but he said its progress depended on the various political viewpoints.

"Political views must be established and acted upon. At the present time we are exchanging views on this subject. Putting (the programme) into action this year is linked totally to political support," Ercel said.
Ercel said that Turkey needs to establish macroeconomic stability in order to make the most of its position in the new world order.
"Primarily, the condition for this is to achieve and maintain macroeconomic stability," he said.
Links with the European Union were a part of Turkey's efforts towards international integration, the central banker said.
"In this connection cultural harmony must be realised with Europe," he said. "Turkey is increasingly taking the road towards more integration with the EU."
He said that Turkey must carry out reforms in education and the social sphere in the coming years to capitalise on the country's potential.
